title: Compose the v4 source-assisted complex word with the PR200 bit supplier: conditional κ = 6.768823e-4
body:
## Result

Conditional κ = 6768823/10^10 = **0.0006768823**, about 1.416% above PR194 (0.0006674324) and 1.819% above PR193.

## What changed

This branch is PR194 (ikeboy) plus my PR200 bit-supplier package plus one commit. PR194 composes icekylinx's PR184 source-assisted complex word, rebuilt on PR168 v4 modules (complex saving 219037/312500000 = 0.0007009184), with my PR189 bit supplier; the bit side binds there. Here `assemble.py` reads the certified bit profile of PR200 instead (`research/paired-cube-diagonal-bit-168/certificate.json`: R = 17,114, W = 20,634, rank mass 1,483,712, deficit 1,936, largest child 60; coarse saving 677773948354561/10^18, effective saving about 0.000677340914792). PR184's `select()` and `assemble()` run unchanged: bad-row allowance 10^-16 with fallback 32 m^2 per edge, coarse saving on the 10^-10 grid, least payable atom on the 10^-12 grid, ordinary leaf 384599/10^10, then the 47-constraint balanced assembly with PR184's finite bridge. The bit branch still binds.

| Version | Complex saving | Bit supplier | Bit effective saving | κ |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR193 | 7.009184e-4 | PR184 | 6.652295e-4 | 6.647872e-4 |
| PR194 | 7.009184e-4 | PR189 | 6.678782e-4 | 6.674324e-4 |
| this PR | 7.009184e-4 | PR200 | 6.773409e-4 | **6.768823e-4** |

The PR200 bit word is PR168 v4's bit graph with a different per-cube local circuit (face diagonals for A[0,0], A[0,1], A[2,0], A[2,1]; direction-0 edges for A[1,·]; fixed-coordinate differences for G[0,1,0]), found by random restarts and coordinate descent with each candidate priced through a full physical pipeline; its carrier matching, gauges, physical layer (7,282 descended frames, 1,760 compensated handoffs) and 34 PR166 terminal sinks are regenerated and independently certified by that package (all 20,668 F2 and defining-integer-decoder columns, exact prime witnesses for all 24,401 used frames, three sink controls rejected). PR200 is based on `main` and vendors the PR168 v4 files it executes; its full 16-group gate and CI pass there.

## Verify

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/source-assisted/requirements-round13.txt
python3 -B research/source-assisted-v4/verify.py
python3 -B research/paired-cube-diagonal-bit-168/verify.py
```

Both pass on Linux at commit `8d8d67bcf69c5ea67d3a29dbc64ba588156d6e8d` (tree `4d07f3f18343da5a0f474d6d830afe64c0c18505`); the second regenerates the bit certificate the assembly reads. The workflow `.github/workflows/source-assisted-v4.yml` runs both. PR194's manifest pins and this workflow are updated for the new bit package; nothing else in the source-assisted packages changes.

## Scope

PR184's validation scope applies to the complex supplier (exact local lifts and contract checks, no globally renumbered scalar transcript, no full Clifford/router replay). The bit supplier keeps PR200's scope. The analytic, recursion, precision, weighted frame, fixed-tape routing, restored-row and all-size interfaces remain assumptions. Like PR194, this branch is on the PR168 v4 lineage and is not directly mergeable onto the current `main`; PR200 itself is.

## Credits

icekylinx (PR184, with GPT-6 Astra and Codex assistance) for the source-assisted method, tools, finite bridge and assembly; Avi Eisenberg / ikeboy (PR191, PR193, PR194, with Claude assistance) for the v4 composition and packaging; eumemic (PR168 v4, with Claude assistance) for the query modules and physical layer; James Chang (PR166) for terminal accumulation. The stronger bit supplier (PR200) is mine, prepared with Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex assistance. This composition changes only which bit certificate is read.
